topIssues.title: Flaky test: FuzzDetectNonBijectivity mutates a non-encoded bit (op-service/eth)
topIssues.author: wwared
topIssues.body:
`FuzzDetectNonBijectivity` (`op-service/eth/blob_test.go`) flips one `sha256(input)`-derived bit of an encoded blob and asserts the decode must change. The two high bits of the blob's first byte are not part of the encoding — `FromData` always writes them as 0, and `ToData` neither validates nor uses them (the first field element is special-cased and `reassembleBytes` masks them off via `& 0b0011_1111`). When the derived flip lands there, the blob still decodes to identical data and `require.NotEqual` fails, even though nothing is wrong.

### Observed failure
- Job: `fuzz-golang-op-service`, branch `develop`: https://circleci.com/gh/ethereum-optimism/optimism/5250793
```
--- FAIL: FuzzDetectNonBijectivity (40.40s)
    --- FAIL: FuzzDetectNonBijectivity (0.00s)
        blob_test.go:172: Should not be: hexutil.Bytes{0xea, 0x2b, 0x58, ...}
```
Reproducing input flips bit 6 of `blob[0]` — a no-op on decode.

### Cause / scope
This is a too-strong test invariant, not a production bug: only those two non-encoded bits trigger it. Distinct from the closed #20936 (a non-determinism hang, fixed by #20940 — which is what activated this assertion).

### Fix
Test-only: don't mutate the two non-encoded high bits of `blob[0]`. No production behavior changes.

topIssues.title: kona-sp1: dedup derivation prologue against the native fault-proof path
topIssues.author: digorithm
topIssues.body:
Follow-up to #18494. That issue deduped the derivation *loop* (`advance_to_target`); this one covers the derivation *prologue* that precedes it, which is still duplicated across the native fault-proof and kona-sp1 paths.

## Problem

The prologue that sets up derivation is near-identical in (at least) two places, and consensus-critical:

- kona-sp1: [`sp1/crates/client/src/witness/executor.rs:33` (`get_inputs_for_pipeline`)](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/89e14a66eff1e6663233b76f5ad75346b270dd53/rust/kona/sp1/crates/client/src/witness/executor.rs#L33)
- native single-chain: [`bin/client/src/single.rs:43` (`run`, prologue portion)](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/89e14a66eff1e6663233b76f5ad75346b270dd53/rust/kona/bin/client/src/single.rs#L43)

Both perform the same sequence:

1. `BootInfo::load`
2. `fetch_safe_head_hash` (see #21657)
3. build `OracleL1ChainProvider` / `OracleL2ChainProvider`
4. `header_by_hash` + `Sealed::new_unchecked` for the safe head
5. reject `claimed_l2_block_number < safe_head.number`
6. trace-extension short-circuit on `claimed_l2_block_number == safe_head.number` (identical `"Trace extension detected. State transition is already agreed upon."` log + the agreed==claimed output-root check)
7. `new_oracle_pipeline_cursor` + `set_cursor`

The cursor-construction tail (steps 6-7) also recurs in the interop path ([`bin/client/src/interop/transition.rs:117`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/89e14a66eff1e6663233b76f5ad75346b270dd53/rust/kona/bin/client/src/interop/transition.rs#L117)) and the host ([`bin/host/src/interop/handler.rs:578`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/89e14a66eff1e6663233b76f5ad75346b270dd53/rust/kona/bin/host/src/interop/handler.rs#L578)).

Duplicating the block-number validation and the trace-extension short-circuit across paths is the same drift risk #18494 addressed for the loop: a fix or hardening applied to one path can silently miss the other.

## Proposed change

Extract a shared prologue helper into `kona-proof` that, given an oracle + boot info, performs steps 1-7 and returns either:

- a "trace extension / zero-step" signal (claim already agreed, no derivation needed), or
- the constructed `(cursor, l1_provider, l2_provider)` ready for pipeline construction.

Then:

- `get_inputs_for_pipeline` (kona-sp1) becomes a thin adapter over it.
- `single.rs::run` calls it, mapping the signal to its `FaultProofProgramError` / `anyhow` error shapes as needed.

## Design considerations

- The two callers differ in shape today: kona-sp1 returns `(BootInfo, Option<(cursor, l1, l2)>)` and builds the pipeline separately; `single.rs` builds inline and uses `FaultProofProgramError` (vs kona-sp1's `anyhow`). The shared helper should return a neutral result the caller maps to its own error type.
- Keep the existing kona-sp1 tests (`get_inputs_for_pipeline_short_circuits_zero_step_claim`, `get_inputs_for_pipeline_rejects_zero_step_root_mismatch`) green; add native-path coverage for the shared helper.
- Interop prologue is a variant (different `BootInfo`/`PreState`); folding it in is a stretch goal, not required for the first pass.

## Acceptance

- One shared prologue helper in a library crate; `get_inputs_for_pipeline` and `single.rs::run` both delegate to it with no duplicated validation/short-circuit logic.
- Existing tests preserved; native + kona-sp1 range guest build and pass.
- Depends on / pairs well with #21657 (shared `fetch_safe_head_hash`).

## Scope

Larger than #21657 and touches consensus-critical validation shared by the native fault-proof program: needs review, not a drive-by.

topIssues.title: kona-sp1: hoist fetch_safe_head_hash into kona-proof (dedup)
topIssues.author: digorithm
topIssues.body:
Follow-up to #18494 (same dedup theme: kona-sp1 was vendored wholesale from op-succinct and carries copies of kona logic).

## Problem

`fetch_safe_head_hash` exists as three byte-identical copies:

- [`sp1/crates/client/src/client.rs:19`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/89e14a66eff1e6663233b76f5ad75346b270dd53/rust/kona/sp1/crates/client/src/client.rs#L19) (`pub(crate)`)
- [`bin/client/src/single.rs:194`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/89e14a66eff1e6663233b76f5ad75346b270dd53/rust/kona/bin/client/src/single.rs#L194) (`pub`)

Each also carries its own duplicate test (`sp1 .../client.rs` tests + [`bin/client/tests/output_root.rs`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/89e14a66eff1e6663233b76f5ad75346b270dd53/rust/kona/bin/client/tests/output_root.rs)).

The reason it was never deduped: the "canonical" copy lives in a **binary** crate (`bin/client`), so it cannot be imported. It is pure oracle logic (`HintType::StartingL2Output` hint + `get_exact` + output-version check), with no fault-proof-specific dependency.

## Proposed change

- Move `fetch_safe_head_hash` into a library crate. Natural home: `kona-proof` (its sibling `new_oracle_pipeline_cursor` already lives in `kona_proof::sync`).
- Update `bin/client/src/single.rs` and `sp1/crates/client` to call the shared function; delete both copies.
- Consolidate the duplicate tests onto the shared location (keep the existing coverage: unknown-output-version rejection and wrong-preimage-length rejection).

## Acceptance

- One definition of `fetch_safe_head_hash` in a library crate; no copies remain in `bin/client` or `sp1/crates/client`.
- Existing tests preserved and passing.
- `bin/client` (native fault-proof) and the kona-sp1 range guest build unchanged.

## Scope

Small, mechanical, low risk. Independent of the larger prologue dedup (separate issue).

topPRs.title: feat(kona-sp1): scaffold super interop programs
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
## Summary

This PR adds the initial SP1 super interop proof shape for ZK dispute games.

It introduces shared public IO types for the unified super-range program and final super-aggregation program, including super-root encoding and final public-value encoding that match the tuple verified by `ZKDisputeGame.prove`.

The output-root range and consolidation proofs are now handled by a single unified super-range program with (optimistic output-root) range and consolidation modes, so aggregation verifies one semantic class of proof with one `range_vkey`.

The guest execution logic is intentionally still incomplete in this PR. The aggregation program accepts the range vkey dynamically for now, and the range/consolidation verification bodies are left as TODOs for the follow-up implementation work.

## Program Input Validation

This PR also introduces logic to validate the program input shape. This validation is complementary to the more involved super-STF operations, ensuring that the super-aggregation program verifies that all required proofs are well-formed and provided.

### Super-range input validation

The unified super-range program first validates the mode-specific input shape.
For range mode, it checks:

- the timestamp span is valid
- chain IDs are non-empty and strictly increasing
- claimed transitions cover exactly every (timestamp, chain_id) pair in span order
- each transition’s timestamp and chain ID match the expected position

For consolidation mode, it checks:

- the timestamp span is valid
- there is one consolidation input per timestamp
- each claimed super-root proof has the expected timestamp
- each super-root proof uses the supported version and ordered chain set
- optimistic blocks are non-empty, strictly ordered, and match the claimed super-root proof’s chain coverage
- every timestamp uses the same chain set

### Super-aggregation input validation

Aggregation validates the declared range public outputs before recursive proof verification.
It checks:

- `starting_super_root_proof` hashes to `starting_root_hash`
- there is at least one range output and one consolidation output
- the disputed interval starts at `starting_super_root.timestamp + 1`
- consolidation outputs cover the full timestamp interval contiguously
- consolidation `previous_super_root` values chain forward from `starting_root_hash`
- the final consolidated root equals `root_claim`
- range outputs cover the same full timestamp interval contiguously
- every range output commits to the same `l1_head` as the game
- every range output’s `previous_super_root` matches the super root before that range
- range optimistic blocks match the corresponding consolidation optimistic blocks timestamp by timestamp
- all range/consolidation outputs use the chain set from the starting super root

## Meta

part of https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21459

topPRs.title: superchain: reject unknown keys when decoding registry configs
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
Follow-up to #21566, which had to hand-add `keep_karst_upgrade_gas` to op-node's registry structs after it was silently dropped: the TOML decoder ignores any key no struct field models. This adds the guard that would have caught it, on both clients.

- **op-node**: `jsonutil.DecodeTOMLStrict` rejects any registry TOML key not represented in the target struct (an `allowUnknown func(string) bool` predicate tolerates specific keys). Chain configs allow nothing — `ChainConfig` models every field; the superchain path allow-lists only the deliberately-unmodeled legacy `protocol_versions_addr`. `TestAllEmbeddedConfigsDecodeStrictly` makes a future registry bump that adds an unmodeled field fail until the struct consumes it.
- **op-node**: extract the registry→`rollup.Config` conversion into `rollupConfigFromRegistry`, separate from the registry lookup. `TestRollupConfigFromRegistry_AllFieldsSet` reflects over the result and fails on any zero field, catching a registry-derived field forgotten in the conversion.
- **kona**: add `deny_unknown_fields` to the top-level `ChainConfig`. Its `HardForkConfig` already had it (so the exact bug couldn't recur there), but the top-level struct silently dropped unknown keys. Also fixes `test_chain_config_unknown_field_json`, which only passed because of an unrelated parse error rather than the unknown key.

No behavior change at the pinned superchain-registry commit — every embedded chain and superchain decodes cleanly (op-node) / the embedded `configs.json` deserializes cleanly (kona). The point is that future schema drift fails loudly instead of being silently dropped.
